narrative.overview: Àmì is a white, open room where the videos do the talking. Every screen is mostly paper white and generous space, and the colour comes from the content itself: creators laughing, jollof steaming, aso-oke at an owambe. The interface stays quiet so the clips can be loud. Each section says one thing. It gets one headline, at most one short line under it, and one action. Media is real photography or moving video, framed in large rounded rectangles that sit inset on the white page rather than bleeding edge to edge. Where text sits on media, a dark scrim keeps it readable, and the type gets big and confident rather than decorated.
keyCharacteristics: White page, generous section spacing, a centred 1240px container.
Bricolage Grotesque headlines, Figtree for everything you read or click.
Real photos and looping muted video as the main visual material.
Ink-black pill buttons on white; white pill buttons on media.
Blue appears only as small marks.

rules.name: The Mark Rule
rules.body: Blue only ever appears as a small mark: a logo accent, a numbered disc, a badge, a focus ring. It never fills a section, a hero or a large button. If blue covers more than a thumbnail's worth of a screen, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Content Is The Colour Rule
rules.body: Backgrounds stay white or media. Don't add tinted panels or gradients to make a section feel colourful; pick a better photo or clip instead.

rules.name: The One Headline Rule
rules.body: A section gets one headline and at most one supporting line. No labels or kickers above headlines, no second sub-heading.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow until it floats over media or responds to a pointer.

dos: Do give every section one headline, one short line and one action.
Do use real photography or looping muted video of Nigerian creators and culture as the main visual material.
Do put a dark scrim (about 50%) under any text that sits on media.
Do keep blue to small marks (The Mark Rule).
Do respect reduced motion: show posters instead of playing video.
donts: Don't fill the page with rows of video cards, receipt-style widgets or paragraphs of explanation; this was rejected as cluttered.
Don't add play buttons, progress bars, "Preview" tags or other player chrome on top of clip tiles.
Don't use monospace type for decoration, or labels and kickers above headlines.
Don't use flat colour fields or gradients where a photo or clip belongs.
Don't float info cards over images ("Tolu earned ₦42,500", "Licence valid…"); both were removed.
Don't add copy, filters or settings nobody asked for; remove before adding.
Don't use sparkle icons; they read as "AI".
